checks.model_quote: The (1+1)-dimensional directed polymer model in Gaussian environment is defined as follows.
checks.theorem_quote: Theorem 8.1. For some universal constant C, we have Var(M) <= Cn/log n.
checks.corrected_statement: For i.i.d. standard Gaussian weights on vertices of the nonnegative quadrant, let M_n be the maximum sum over directed length-n paths from the origin taking up or right steps. The source asks to improve the fluctuation exponent beyond Theorem 8.1's Var(M_n) <= C n/log n. A natural precise power target is: find epsilon>0 and C_epsilon with Var(M_n) <= C_epsilon n^(1-epsilon) for all sufficiently large n. The power target is an interpretation of the source's wording, not a verbatim question.

checks.finding: The 2009 paper gives an n/log n Gaussian bound for fixed diagonal endpoints in general dimension; the 2024 paper studies fixed endpoints and nonnegative weight laws, cites n/log n nearly-Gamma bounds, and reports exact exponent only for integrable weights. Neither is a verified resolution of the source's Gaussian free-endpoint target. Targeted C0120/directed-polymer searches found no entry in the local solved registers or intake D-G status files. This bounded check cannot certify that no later solution or owner-retired result exists.

exact_source_statement: Source Section 12(3): Improve the fluctuation exponent in the Section 8 (1+1)-dimensional Gaussian zero-temperature directed-polymer model beyond its logarithmic correction; proposed quantitative target Var(M_n)=O(n^(1-epsilon)) for some epsilon>0.
intake_mismatch: The 2026-09-07 problems.jsonl C0120 row substitutes Var(log Z_n) and general dimension for source Theorem 8.1's Var(M_n) in 1+1 Gaussian directed last-passage percolation. The 2026-09-07 attempt inherits this mismatch.
